desc: Ideation: shortest-path interdiction via potentials, binary search on D, ≤K vs exactly K equivalence

Formalize and verify the fixed-D min-cut construction: nodes (v,i) for i=1..D; infinite chain edges (v,i+1)→(v,i); force p[1]=0 via (1,i)→T and p[N]=D via S→(N,i); per original edge (u,v): infinite edges (v,i+1)→(u,i) for i=1..D−1 (Lipschitz p[v]≤p[u]+1) and unit edges (v,i)→(u,i) for i=1..D (cost 1 iff p[v]=p[u]+1); multi-edges get separate unit edges
Hand-verify construction on Samples 1–3 (answers 1, 2, 0 all reproduced) and on the potential/duality argument (min #ones = min over potentials of crossing count; dist ≥ D via telescoping)

Implement the complete Python solution: stdin parsing, a Dinic maxflow module, the verified layered min-cut feasibility check feasible(D) = (mincut ≤ K), binary search for the maximal D in [0, min(K, N−1)], and print the answer

Verify implementation against the three samples and brute-force cross-check on tiny random graphs (N≤5, M≤8, enumerate all K-subsets) covering multi-edges, cycles, K=M, K=1, and D=0 cases — all match, with full correctness proof of the potentials ⇔ min-cut equivalence
